messages:
maya: FYI ran into another auth mix-up with the Python async client today. different from the env-rotation ones: happens when tasks use contextvars + shared session.
jonathan: oof, can you paste a tiny repro?
maya: yep. short version: we store a per-coro API key in a contextvar and expect AsyncClient to call an auth provider per-request. instead the library set the header on the global session, so concurrent tasks see the wrong key.
```py
import contextvars, asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient
key_var = contextvars.ContextVar('key')
async def auth_provider():
    return key_var.get()
client = AsyncClient(auth_provider=auth_provider)
async def worker(k):
    key_var.set(k)
    return await client.generate('hey')
# schedule two tasks with different keys -> responses show swapped Authorization headers
```
kevin: that matches a design flaw: we currently mutate session.headers on client init. when auth is dynamic we must inject headers per-request.
alice: typing wise we don't expose an async provider Protocol. the stub uses Callable[[], str] which forces sync providers. IDEs won't flag misuse.
jonathan: proposed fix: (1) accept auth_provider: Optional[Callable[[], Union[str, Awaitable[str]]]] in AsyncClient signature and add overloads in py.typed/stubs. (2) default to per-request header injection if auth_provider is provided or multiple clients exist. (3) add a small integration test with asyncio.gather to catch this.
maya: +1. I sketched a types.Protocol:
```py
from typing import Protocol, Awaitable
class AsyncAuthProvider(Protocol):
    def __call__(self) -> Awaitable[str]: ...
```
jonathan: nice. also we should document the recommended pattern for short-lived vs long-lived clients. sample in quickstarts: "multiple clients with different auth providers -> use per-instance session or per-request auth".
kevin: created ticket INF-839 to track API/stub changes + runtime hotfix. assigned to eng-runtime.
devex-bot: New ticket created <https://redwood.internal/tickets/INF-839> by kevin 1"AsyncClient: support async auth_provider + avoid mutating shared session headers"
maya: temporary workaround: create one client per key and set client._session = aiohttp.ClientSession() to avoid header bleed. ugly but works.
alice: we should block that hack by making private attrs harder to access and then ship the proper fix. also add a deprecation/error if library detects auth_provider used but global session mutable.
jonathan: I pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4256 - changes to async client to use per-request headers and updates types/stubs. test included.
kevin: once merged, please add a one-paragraph note to the Python quickstart and a short example under "auth rotation" showing contextvars + async provider. will reduce support tickets.
maya: happy to validate post-merge. thx team :rocket:
